gloss: to listen; to lend an ear; to heed

definitions.gloss: to listen; to lend an ear; to heed; to pay attention to what someone says
definitions.explanation: To be willing to listen to someone's words, request, or advice. Often used in the negative to mean refusing to listen.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}も{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}さなかった。
{彼|かれ}は{人|ひと}の{忠告|ちゅうこく}に{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}さない。
examples.english: He doesn't heed other people's advice.

examples.japanese: ちょっと{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}してくれませんか。{大事|だいじ}な{話|はなし}があるんです。
examples.english: Could you lend me your ear for a moment? I have something important to tell you.

notes:
Literally "to lend one's ear." Very commonly used in the negative ({耳|みみ}を{貸|か}さない) to describe someone who refuses to listen to advice, warnings, or requests.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {耳|みみ}を{貸|か}さない: won't listen, refuses to heed
- {耳|みみ}を{貸|か}してくれる: to be willing to listen
- ちょっと{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}して: lend me your ear for a sec (casual request)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {忠告|ちゅうこく}に{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}す: to heed advice
- {意見|いけん}に{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}す: to listen to opinions
- {訴|うった}えに{耳|みみ}を{貸|か}す: to listen to an appeal

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {耳|みみ}を{傾|かたむ}ける: to incline one's ear — more formal and literary; implies careful, attentive listening
- {聞|き}く{耳|みみ}を{持|も}たない: to refuse to listen at all — stronger refusal than {耳|みみ}を{貸|か}さない
